notes: The guard exists because compliance on a no-interval action does not clear its old limit (advanceDue returns early), so simply removing the guard would turn every such action Overdue on its stale date. A fix needs compliance to clear (or stamp) the satisfied limits so that a limit present after the latest compliance counts. staleInitialLimits() does not flag these actions either (it requires an interval), so nothing on screen tells the user the entered date is ignored.
title: A repeating AD action with no fixed interval ignores any due date, hours, cycles or landings entered after its first compliance: it reads "Due not set" forever and never becomes Due soon or Overdue, never grounds the aircraft and never alerts

Status reads Due soon. 2. Record compliance dated 2026-11-01. Status becomes 'Due not set' (the old 2026-11-30 date stays on the action). 3. Edit the AD, set the action's next due date to 2027-11-30, give a reason, save. 4. Look at the AD register, AD details, aircraft status, Overview alerts and dispatch gate on any later date, including after 2027-11-30.
